summary: Two Python services on EKS with zero-code OpenTelemetry: orders calls inventory over HTTP with a 500 ms timeout, inventory has 4 worker threads at 40 ms a request. An open-loop load of 60 orders a second runs for 170 s, and at second 30 inventory slows to 2 s a request for 20 s. reproduce.sh runs instant retries (up to 3 more, no wait); fix.sh runs exponential backoff with full jitter and a 10% retry budget, with fresh pods, the same load and the same slowdown. analyze.py counts failed orders, recovery to 95% success, calls per order and inventory throughput in the 120 s after the slowdown, and fix.sh reads the same windows back from Splunk APM.
expected: reproduce.sh starts healthy (at least 95% success before the slowdown), shows failed orders after the slowdown, then HERO_RESULT: reproduced. fix.sh starts healthy, recovers to 95% success within 120 s of the slowdown ending, reads both windows back from Splunk APM, then HERO_RESULT: fixed. Whether instant retries recover is the measured result, not a condition.

# Retry storm after a slowdown, seen in Splunk APM

Two Python services on EKS: `orders` takes an order and calls `inventory` over HTTP with a 500 ms timeout. Both run with
zero-code OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry-instrument`) and send traces to the Splunk OTel Collector. `inventory` has 4 worker
threads and takes 40 ms a request, so it can finish about 100 a second.

An open-loop load sends 60 orders a second for 170 s. At second 30 it asks inventory for a 20 s slowdown: every request takes
2 s. After that inventory is healthy again. Each run gets fresh pods and its own order numbers.

| Run | Retry setting in `orders` |
| --- | --- |
| `naive` (`reproduce.sh`) | retry a failed call at once, up to 3 more times |
| `budget` (`fix.sh`) | retry up to 3 more times with exponential backoff and full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 2 s), only while a retry budget allows: each order adds 0.1 of a retry |

`analyze.sh` reads the load output, the orders log and the inventory log for each run and prints, for the 120 s after the
slowdown ended: failed orders, whether and when success got back to 95% for 5 s in a row, inventory calls per order, and
requests inventory finished per second. `fix.sh` then reads the same windows back from Splunk APM (`service.request.count`
for `orders` and `inventory`, all requests and errors).

- `check.sh`: the free check, the same two runs in Docker with an OTLP sink instead of Splunk.
- `lib.sh`: the clock, starting a run, the load and the report. `splunk.sh`: the Splunk reads.

The slowdown is simulated, and this is one load level, one timeout and one dependency. The backlog of requests clients
already gave up on still has to drain; server-side load shedding isn't tested here.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reads one run's three logs and prints the counts, raw first, then HERO_MEASURE lines. Code only, no model.
# Usage: bash analyze.sh <run label> <load output> <orders log> <inventory log>
exec python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import sys, re, collections
label, load_f, orders_f, inv_f = sys.argv[1:5]
WINDOW, CONTROL = 120, 30
lines = open(load_f).read().splitlines()
start = int(re.search(r"LOAD start=(\d+)", "\n".join(lines))[1])
sl = re.search(r"SLOWDOWN start=(\d+) end=(\d+) second=(\d+) seconds=(\d+)", "\n".join(lines))
slow_at, slow_s = int(sl[3]), int(sl[4]); end_s = slow_at + slow_s
per = {}
for l in lines:
    m = re.match(r"LOAD second=(\d+) ok=(\d+) failed=(\d+)", l)
    if m: per[int(m[1])] = (int(m[2]), int(m[3]))
sent = int(re.search(r"LOAD end=\d+ sent=(\d+)", "\n".join(lines))[1])
before = [per.get(s, (0, 0)) for s in range(slow_at - CONTROL, slow_at)]
b_ok, b_all = sum(o for o, f in before), sum(o + f for o, f in before)
during = [per.get(s, (0, 0)) for s in range(slow_at, end_s)]
d_fail, d_all = sum(f for o, f in during), sum(o + f for o, f in during)
after = [(s, *per.get(s, (0, 0))) for s in range(end_s, end_s + WINDOW)]
a_fail, a_all = sum(f for s, o, f in after), sum(o + f for s, o, f in after)
recovered_at = None
for i in range(len(after) - 4):
    if all(after[j][1] + after[j][2] > 0 and after[j][1] / (after[j][1] + after[j][2]) >= 0.95 for j in range(i, i + 5)):
        recovered_at = after[i][0] - end_s; break
print(f"{label}: load started {start}, slowdown from second {slow_at} for {slow_s} s, watched seconds {end_s} to {end_s + WINDOW - 1}")
print(f"{label}: success per 10 s after the slowdown (ok/sent): " + " ".join(f"{sum(x[1] for x in after[i:i+10])}/{sum(x[1]+x[2] for x in after[i:i+10])}" for i in range(0, WINDOW, 10)))
print(f"{label}: before the slowdown {b_ok} of {b_all} orders succeeded")
print(f"{label}: during the slowdown {d_fail} of {d_all} orders failed")
print(f"{label}: after the slowdown {a_fail} of {a_all} orders failed")
print(f"{label}: back to 95% success for 5 s in a row: " + (f"{recovered_at} s after the slowdown ended" if recovered_at is not None else f"not within {WINDOW} s"))
# Calls per order from the orders log, for orders placed in the watched window.
w0, w1 = start + end_s, start + end_s + WINDOW
calls = orders = 0
for l in open(orders_f):
    m = re.match(r"ORDER \d+ ok=(\d) attempts=(\d+) t=(\d+)", l)
    if m and w0 <= int(m[3]) < w1:
        calls += int(m[2]); orders += 1
cpo = calls / orders if orders else 0
print(f"{label}: orders log, {orders} orders in the window made {calls} inventory calls, {cpo:.2f} per order")
handled = [int(m[2]) for m in re.finditer(r"INVENTORY t=(\d+) handled=(\d+)", open(inv_f).read()) if w0 <= int(m[1]) < w1]
hps = sum(handled) / len(handled) if handled else 0
print(f"{label}: inventory finished {sum(handled)} requests in {len(handled)} s of the window, {hps:.1f} a second")
pct = lambda a, b: f"{100 * a / b:.1f}" if b else "null"
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: orders_sent[{label}]={sent}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: orders_success_before_pct[{label}]={pct(b_ok, b_all)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_during_slowdown[{label}]={d_fail}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_after_slowdown[{label}]={a_fail}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: recovered_within_window[{label}]={1 if recovered_at is not None else 0}")
if recovered_at is not None:
    print(f"HERO_MEASURE: seconds_to_recover[{label}]={recovered_at}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: attempts_per_order_after[{label}]={cpo:.2f}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: inventory_handled_per_second_after[{label}]={hps:.1f}")
with open(f"window-{label}.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write(f"{w0} {w1} {a_fail} {a_all} {1 if recovered_at is not None else 0}\n")
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, on a GitHub runner with Docker, before AWS is paid for. It runs the lab's real code (the same files the
# manifests carry) in python:3.12-slim with the pinned packages and zero-code OpenTelemetry, both retry modes, with the
# same load and slowdown. Kubernetes and Splunk are not tested here. The naive result is printed, not asserted: that is
# the lab's finding. The budget run must recover, because that is the fix the article shows.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/app c/load c/venv

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
for k in ("requirements.txt", "inventory.py", "orders.py"):
    open(f"c/app/{k}", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", k))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY
IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ "]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== One virtualenv with the pinned packages, as the build Job makes it"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/app:/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  python -m venv /lab/venv && /lab/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r /app/requirements.txt &&
  /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE "^(flask|waitress|requests|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|instrumentation-flask|instrumentation-requests))=="'

# A tiny OTLP sink stands in for the Collector: it answers 200 and counts the trace exports it receives.
cat > c/sink.py <<'PY'
import http.server, threading
n = {"posts": 0}
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))); n["posts"] += 1
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Length", "0"); self.end_headers()
    def do_GET(self):
        b = str(n["posts"]).encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b)
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 4318), H).serve_forever()
PY
OTEL="-e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://sink:4318 -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf -e OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none -e OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1"
start() {   # service, extra env...
  local s=$1; shift
  docker rm -f "$s" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name "$s" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/app:/lab/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv:ro" $OTEL -e "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=$s" "$@" \
    "$IMAGE" /lab/venv/bin/opentelemetry-instrument /lab/venv/bin/python "/lab/app/$s.py" >/dev/null
}
ready() {   # service, port
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker exec "$1" /lab/venv/bin/python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:$2/healthz', timeout=2)" 2>/dev/null && return 0; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1
}

run() {   # mode, first order
  echo "== $1"
  docker rm -f sink >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name sink --network lab -v "$PWD/c/sink.py:/sink.py:ro" "$IMAGE" python /sink.py >/dev/null
  start inventory -e THREADS=4 -e WORK_MS=40
  start orders -e THREADS=400 -e INVENTORY_URL=http://inventory:8081 -e "RETRY_MODE=$1"
  ready inventory 8081; ready orders 8080
  docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e RATE=60 -e LOAD_SECONDS=170 -e "FIRST=$2" \
    -e ORDERS_HOST=orders -e INVENTORY_HOST=inventory -e SLOW_AT=30 -e SLOW_SECONDS=20 -e SLOW_MS=2000 "$IMAGE" python /load/load.py > "c/load-$1.txt"
  docker logs orders > "c/orders-$1.log" 2>&1
  docker logs inventory > "c/inventory-$1.log" 2>&1
  sleep 6   # one more export interval
  posts=$(docker exec sink python -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:4318/').read().decode())")
  echo "$1: OTLP trace exports the sink received from both services: $posts"
  [ "${posts:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: zero-code OpenTelemetry exported nothing"; exit 1; }
  docker rm -f orders inventory sink >/dev/null
  bash analyze.sh "$1" "c/load-$1.txt" "c/orders-$1.log" "c/inventory-$1.log" | tee "c/report-$1.txt"
  grep -q "orders_success_before_pct\[$1\]=\(9[5-9]\|100\)" "c/report-$1.txt" || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the $1 run started unhealthy"; exit 1; }
}

run naive 1
run budget 20001
grep -q 'recovered_within_window\[budget\]=1' c/report-budget.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the budget run didn't recover within 120 s"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'failed_orders_after_slowdown\[naive\]=[1-9]' c/report-naive.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the naive run had no failures after the slowdown, so there is nothing to show"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: one setting changed. RETRY_MODE=budget makes orders retry with exponential backoff and full jitter (base 100 ms,
# cap 2 s), and only while a retry budget allows (each order adds 0.1 of a retry, so retries stay near 10% of calls).
# Same code, same image, same load, same slowdown. Then the same windows of both runs are read back from Splunk APM.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 830 not_fixed

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"

echo "== 1. The before-check: the cluster's own data reaches Splunk"
wait_cluster "$(cap 120 650)"
echo "cluster metric time series in Splunk: ${cluster:-0}"
[ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no cluster data reached Splunk, so a zero here would prove nothing"

echo "== 2. The one change: backoff with full jitter and a retry budget"
start_run budget 120
load_run budget "$(cap 240 250)"
report budget

echo "== 3. The same windows in Splunk APM: 120 s after each slowdown ended"
sleep 45   # APM metrics land a little after the spans
for m in naive budget; do
  read w0 w1 _ _ _ < "window-$m.txt" || fail "no window recorded for $m"
  total=$(apm_count orders all "$w0" "$w1"); errors=$(apm_count orders true "$w0" "$w1"); inv=$(apm_count inventory all "$w0" "$w1")
  echo "$m in Splunk APM, seconds $w0 to $w1: orders requests $total, of them errors $errors; inventory requests $inv"
  pct=$(awk -v e="$errors" -v t="$total" 'BEGIN { if (t > 0) printf "%.1f", 100 * e / t; else print "null" }')
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_orders_error_pct_after[$m]=$pct"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_inventory_requests_after[$m]=${inv:-null}"
  [ "$m" = budget ] && budget_total=$total
done

# The gate is that the budget run started healthy, recovered inside the window, and Splunk returned the same window.
if [ "${recovered:-0}" = 1 ] && [ "${budget_total:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  emit fixed
else
  emit not_fixed
fi

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-src
  namespace: demo
data:
  requirements.txt: |
    flask==3.1.3
    waitress==3.0.2
    requests==2.34.2
    opentelemetry-distro==0.66b2
    opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.45.2
    opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask==0.66b2
    opentelemetry-instrumentation-requests==0.66b2

  inventory.py: |
    # inventory: reserves stock. A fixed pool of sync workers, each request holds one for WORK_MS. During a brownout every
    # request takes BROWNOUT_MS instead, as if a dependency were stuck. Requests a client already gave up on are still worked,
    # because a sync worker can't tell, which is what makes a backlog expensive.
    import os, threading, time
    from flask import Flask, request
    app = Flask(__name__)
    WORK_MS = int(os.environ.get("WORK_MS", "40"))
    STATE = os.environ.get("BROWNOUT_FILE", "/tmp/brownout")    # shared by every worker process
    stats = {"handled": 0}
    lock = threading.Lock()

    @app.post("/admin/brownout")
    def brownout():
        secs, delay = float(request.args.get("seconds", "30")), int(request.args.get("delay_ms", "2000"))
        until = time.time() + secs
        with open(STATE, "w") as f:
            f.write(f"{until} {delay}")
        print(f"BROWNOUT start seconds={secs:g} delay_ms={delay} until={until:.0f}", flush=True)
        return {"until": until}

    def current_delay():
        try:
            until, delay = open(STATE).read().split()
            return int(delay) if time.time() < float(until) else WORK_MS
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return WORK_MS

    @app.get("/reserve/<int:order>")
    def reserve(order):
        time.sleep(current_delay() / 1000)
        with lock:
            stats["handled"] += 1
        return {"order": order, "reserved": True}

    def reporter():
        # One line a second: requests finished in that second. Single process, so this is the whole service.
        last = 0
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
            with lock:
                now = stats["handled"]
            print(f"INVENTORY t={int(time.time())} handled={now - last}", flush=True)
            last = now

    threading.Thread(target=reporter, daemon=True).start()

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        return "ok"

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        # waitress: one process, a fixed pool of worker threads and a queue in front of them. No fork, so zero-code
        # OpenTelemetry works unchanged.
        import logging
        from waitress import serve
        logging.getLogger("waitress.queue").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
        serve(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8081")), threads=int(os.environ.get("THREADS", "4")),
              connection_limit=900, backlog=2048, channel_timeout=120)

  orders.py: |
    # orders: takes an order and reserves it in inventory with a 500 ms timeout. RETRY_MODE decides what happens on a failure:
    #   naive  - retry at once, up to RETRIES more times
    #   budget - retry with exponential backoff and full jitter, and only while the retry budget allows: each order adds
    #            BUDGET_RATIO of a token, each retry spends one, so retries stay a small share of traffic
    import os, random, threading, time
    import requests
    from flask import Flask
    app = Flask(__name__)
    INVENTORY = os.environ.get("INVENTORY_URL", "http://localhost:8081")
    MODE = os.environ.get("RETRY_MODE", "naive")
    RETRIES = int(os.environ.get("RETRIES", "3"))
    TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("TIMEOUT_S", "0.5"))
    BASE, CAP = float(os.environ.get("BACKOFF_BASE_S", "0.1")), float(os.environ.get("BACKOFF_CAP_S", "2"))
    RATIO, MAX_TOKENS = float(os.environ.get("BUDGET_RATIO", "0.1")), float(os.environ.get("BUDGET_MAX", "10"))
    tokens, lock = [MAX_TOKENS], threading.Lock()
    session = requests.Session()
    session.mount("http://", requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=4, pool_maxsize=256))

    def may_retry():
        if MODE != "budget":
            return True
        with lock:
            if tokens[0] >= 1:
                tokens[0] -= 1
                return True
            return False

    import logging
    log = logging.getLogger("orders"); logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")

    @app.post("/orders/<int:order>")
    def place(order):
        ok, attempts = reserve_with_retries(order)
        log.info("ORDER %d ok=%d attempts=%d t=%d", order, ok, attempts, int(time.time()))
        return ({"order": order, "attempts": attempts}, 200) if ok else ({"order": order, "failed": True}, 503)

    def reserve_with_retries(order):
        if MODE == "budget":
            with lock:
                tokens[0] = min(MAX_TOKENS, tokens[0] + RATIO)
        for attempt in range(RETRIES + 1):
            try:
                r = session.get(f"{INVENTORY}/reserve/{order}", timeout=TIMEOUT)
                if r.status_code == 200:
                    return True, attempt + 1
            except requests.RequestException:
                pass
            if attempt == RETRIES or not may_retry():
                break
            if MODE == "budget":
                time.sleep(random.uniform(0, min(CAP, BASE * 2 ** attempt)))
        return False, attempt + 1

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        return "ok"

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        import logging
        from waitress import serve
        logging.getLogger("waitress.queue").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
        serve(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8080")), threads=int(os.environ.get("THREADS", "400")),
              connection_limit=900, backlog=2048, channel_timeout=120)

---
# Builds one virtualenv on the app node with pinned packages, once. Both services run from it, in every run.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: build
  namespace: demo
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 420
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      volumes:
        - name: src
          configMap:
            name: app-src
        - name: lab
          hostPath:
            path: /opt/lab
            type: DirectoryOrCreate
      containers:
        - name: build
          image: python:3.12-slim
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: src, mountPath: /src, readOnly: true }
            - { name: lab, mountPath: /lab }
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -e
              rm -rf /lab/venv /lab/app && mkdir -p /lab/app
              cp /src/inventory.py /src/orders.py /src/requirements.txt /lab/app/
              python -m venv /lab/venv
              for i in 1 2 3; do /lab/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r /lab/app/requirements.txt && break; echo "pip attempt $i failed"; sleep 10; done
              /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE '^(flask|waitress|requests|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|exporter-otlp-proto-http|instrumentation-flask|instrumentation-requests))=='
              sha256sum /lab/app/*.py

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Open-loop load: RATE orders a second whatever happens, as real users keep arriving. At SLOW_AT seconds it asks
    # inventory for a slowdown of SLOW_SECONDS, then keeps sending. Prints one line per second, with epoch times.
    import os, threading, time, http.client
    RATE, SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("RATE", "60")), int(os.environ.get("LOAD_SECONDS", "170"))
    HOST, PORT = os.environ.get("ORDERS_HOST", "localhost"), int(os.environ.get("ORDERS_PORT", "8080"))
    INV, INV_PORT = os.environ.get("INVENTORY_HOST", "localhost"), int(os.environ.get("INVENTORY_PORT", "8081"))
    FIRST = int(os.environ.get("FIRST", "1"))
    SLOW_AT, SLOW_S, SLOW_MS = int(os.environ.get("SLOW_AT", "30")), int(os.environ.get("SLOW_SECONDS", "20")), int(os.environ.get("SLOW_MS", "2000"))
    res, lock = {}, threading.Lock()

    def one(n, sec):
        ok = False
        try:
            c = http.client.HTTPConnection(HOST, PORT, timeout=5)
            c.request("POST", f"/orders/{n}")
            ok = c.getresponse().status == 200
            c.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        with lock:
            res.setdefault(sec, [0, 0])[0 if ok else 1] += 1

    def slowdown():
        c = http.client.HTTPConnection(INV, INV_PORT, timeout=10)
        c.request("POST", f"/admin/brownout?seconds={SLOW_S}&delay_ms={SLOW_MS}")
        print("SLOWDOWN reply", c.getresponse().status, flush=True)

    t0 = time.time(); n = FIRST
    print(f"LOAD start={t0:.0f} rate={RATE} seconds={SECONDS} first={FIRST}", flush=True)
    for sec in range(SECONDS):
        if sec == SLOW_AT:
            print(f"SLOWDOWN start={time.time():.0f} end={time.time() + SLOW_S:.0f} second={SLOW_AT} seconds={SLOW_S} delay_ms={SLOW_MS}", flush=True)
            threading.Thread(target=slowdown, daemon=True).start()
        for i in range(RATE):
            threading.Thread(target=one, args=(n, sec), daemon=True).start(); n += 1
            time.sleep(max(0, t0 + sec + (i + 1) / RATE - time.time()))
    time.sleep(6)
    for sec in range(SECONDS):
        ok, bad = res.get(sec, [0, 0])
        print(f"LOAD second={sec} ok={ok} failed={bad}")
    print(f"LOAD end={time.time():.0f} sent={n - FIRST} ok={sum(v[0] for v in res.values())} failed={sum(v[1] for v in res.values())}")

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: RATE, value: "60" }
        - { name: LOAD_SECONDS, value: "170" }
        - { name: FIRST, value: "FIRST" }
        - { name: ORDERS_HOST, value: "orders" }
        - { name: INVENTORY_HOST, value: "inventory" }
        - { name: SLOW_AT, value: "30" }
        - { name: SLOW_SECONDS, value: "20" }
        - { name: SLOW_MS, value: "2000" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }

# Shared by reproduce.sh and fix.sh: the clock, starting a run, the load and the per-run report. Sourced, never run alone.
# One run = fresh orders and inventory pods with one RETRY_MODE, 170 s of open-loop load at 60 orders a second, and a
# 20 s inventory slowdown at second 30 that the load pod itself asks for. analyze.sh turns the three logs into counts.
export LC_ALL=C

start_clock() {   # seconds allowed, the result to print on failure. Every wait is capped so a result always prints.
  START=$(date +%s); LIMIT=$1; FAILED=$2; HERO_DONE=0
  trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $FAILED"; }' EXIT
}
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit "$FAILED"; exit 0; }

newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }
why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -6; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -8 | cut -c1-180; kubectl -n demo logs deploy/"$1" --tail=20 | cut -c1-200; }

# Each run has its own order numbers, so the orders log can't mix runs: naive 1-10200, budget 20001-30200.
first_order() { case "$1" in naive) echo 1 ;; budget) echo 20001 ;; esac; }

# Fresh pods for both services with one retry mode, then proof of what each pod really runs.
start_run() {   # mode, seconds allowed
  kubectl -n demo set env deployment/orders "RETRY_MODE=$1" "LAB_RUN=$1" >/dev/null || fail "could not set orders"
  kubectl -n demo set env deployment/inventory "LAB_RUN=$1" >/dev/null || fail "could not set inventory"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why inventory; fail "inventory did not roll out"; }
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why orders; fail "orders did not roll out"; }
  local s p
  for s in inventory orders; do
    p=$(newest "$s")
    echo "$s $p image $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
    kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -- env | grep -E '^(RETRY_MODE|THREADS|WORK_MS|INVENTORY_URL|OTEL_SERVICE_NAME|OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES)=' | sed 's/^/  /'
    kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -- sha256sum "/lab/app/$s.py" | sed 's/^/  /'
  done
  [ "$(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -- printenv RETRY_MODE)" = "$1" ] || fail "orders is not in $1 mode"
  echo "orders retry settings: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -- sh -c 'grep -E "^(RETRIES|TIMEOUT|BASE, CAP|RATIO, MAX_TOKENS) " /lab/app/orders.py' | tr '\n' ';')"
}

# The load pod sends 60 orders a second for 170 s and asks inventory for the slowdown at second 30.
load_run() {   # mode, seconds allowed
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e "s/value: \"FIRST\"/value: \"$(first_order "$1")\"/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$2s" >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; why orders; fail "the load did not finish"; }
  kubectl -n demo logs load > "load-$1.txt"
  kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest orders)" > "orders-$1.log" 2>/dev/null
  kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest inventory)" > "inventory-$1.log" 2>/dev/null
  grep -E '^(LOAD start|SLOWDOWN|LOAD end)' "load-$1.txt"
  grep -c '^LOAD second' "load-$1.txt" | sed 's/^/per-second lines: /'
}

report() {   # mode. Sets before_pct, recovered and failed_after from analyze.sh's output.
  bash analyze.sh "$1" "load-$1.txt" "orders-$1.log" "inventory-$1.log" | tee "report-$1.txt"
  before_pct=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: orders_success_before_pct\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")
  recovered=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: recovered_within_window\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")
  failed_after=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_after_slowdown\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")
  awk -v p="${before_pct:-0}" 'BEGIN { exit !(p >= 95) }' || fail "the $1 run started unhealthy: ${before_pct:-no} % success before the slowdown"
  # The positive control for the slowdown itself: if no order failed during it, a recovery would prove nothing.
  [ "$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_during_slowdown\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || fail "no order failed during the $1 slowdown, so it had no effect"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: instant retries. orders calls inventory with a 500 ms timeout and retries a failed call at once, up to 3 more
# times. Open-loop load of 60 orders a second; at second 30 inventory slows to 2 s a request for 20 s, then is healthy.
# Measures whether orders come back, and what inventory is doing meanwhile.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh

start_clock 810 not_reproduced

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes -o wide || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" || true

# The services stay on one node and the load on the other, in both runs.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE"
echo "load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] && [ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "the Splunk settings are not set"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1), the same in both runs"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" || fail "collector agent not ready"

echo "== 3. Building one virtualenv with pinned packages on the app node"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
state=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 360 330)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  state=$(kubectl -n demo get job build -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$state" in *Complete*|*Failed*) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build --tail=20 2>/dev/null || true
case "$state" in *Complete*) ;; *) kubectl -n demo describe job build | tail -15; fail "the build did not finish: ${state:-still running}" ;; esac
echo "build took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying inventory and orders with zero-code OpenTelemetry"
sed -e "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" -e "s/LAB_ENV/$LAB_NAME/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the services"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 290)s" >/dev/null || { why inventory; fail "inventory did not start"; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 280)s" >/dev/null || { why orders; fail "orders did not start"; }

echo "== 5. Instant retries: the slowdown at second 30, then 120 s to watch"
start_run naive 120
load_run naive "$(cap 240 15)"
report naive
[ "${failed_after:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no order failed after the slowdown, so there is nothing to fix"

emit reproduced

# Splunk Observability Cloud reads for fix.sh. Sourced, never run alone. Needs SPLUNK_REALM and SPLUNK_API_TOKEN.
# Every SignalFlow program sent is printed, and its points are summed over one window.
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
STREAM="https://stream.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

wait_cluster() {   # seconds. Sets cluster to how many of the cluster's series Splunk holds.
  local t0=$(date +%s); cluster=0
  while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$1" ]; do
    cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
    sleep 15
  done
}

# SignalFlow answers as a stream of events. This prints one value per point between start and stop, summed across series.
signalflow() {   # program, start ms, stop ms, resolution ms
  curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data-binary "$1" \
    "$STREAM/v2/signalflow/execute?start=$2&stop=$3&resolution=${4:-10000}&immediate=true" 2>/dev/null |
    awk '/^event:/ { if (b != "") print e "\t" b; e = $2; b = ""; next }
         /^data:/  { sub(/^data: ?/, ""); b = b $0; next }
         END       { if (b != "") print e "\t" b }' |
    jq -Rr --argjson from "$2" --argjson to "$3" 'split("\t") | select(.[0] == "data") | (.[1] | fromjson? // {})
      | select(.logicalTimestampMs >= $from and .logicalTimestampMs < $to) | "\(.logicalTimestampMs) \([.data[]?.value // empty] | add // 0)"' 2>/dev/null
}

# APM request counts for one service in one window, all requests or errors only. Prints the per-10 s points to stderr.
apm_count() {   # service, errors: all|true, start s, stop s
  local f="filter('sf_environment', '$LAB_NAME') and filter('sf_service', '$1')" try n
  [ "$2" = true ] && f="$f and filter('sf_error', 'true')"
  local prog="data('service.request.count', filter=$f, rollup='sum').sum().publish('n')"
  echo "  program: $prog" >&2
  for try in 1 2 3; do   # a stream can come back empty once, so an empty read is asked again
    signalflow "$prog" "$(( $3 * 1000 ))" "$(( $4 * 1000 ))" > "sf-$1-$2.txt"
    n=$(awk '{t += $2} END {printf "%.0f", t}' "sf-$1-$2.txt")
    [ -s "sf-$1-$2.txt" ] && break
    echo "  read $try came back empty; reading again" >&2; sleep 10
  done
  echo "  $1 $2 from $3 to $4: $(awk '{printf "%s ", $2}' "sf-$1-$2.txt")" >&2
  echo "${n:-0}"
}
